html:
A mass campaign launched by the Indian National Congress on 8 August 1942, in Bombay, demanding that Britain leave India at once. Gandhi told the crowd to "do or die".

It came during World War II, after the Cripps mission of March 1942 offered only post-war self-rule, and with Japan at India's border in Burma. Britain had also brought India into the war without asking.

Within hours of the resolution, Gandhi and the whole Congress leadership were arrested, and the party was banned. With no one to guide it, the movement turned wild, with strikes, attacks on railways, police posts and telegraph lines, and parallel governments in places such as Midnapore and Satara. The Raj answered with force. About 100,000 were arrested and many shot, and it had put the revolt down by 1944.

The Muslim League and the Communists stayed out. With Congress in jail, Jinnah used the time to build the League's base. The Bengal famine came the next year. Britain began to see that it could not hold India much longer.
sum: A mass campaign launched by the Indian National Congress on 8 August 1942, in Bombay, demanding that Britain leave India at once. Gandhi told the crowd to "do or die".
